answer: Every agent hangs on a trellis of mutual attestations: to join, an identity must hold one ivory seal, minted only by a memory-hard sequential proof salted with its own address, so proofs cannot be shared across clones. The tide of stake flows along trellis edges, each carrying a joint bond: if one member of a cluster is caught cheating, the whole cluster is slashed in proportion to the square of its size. N clones therefore pay roughly N squared in lost bonds plus N fresh proofs, while an honest singleton pays one proof and one bond. Sybil scale becomes its own punishment.
